## Using the format

```yaml
format: letter-pdf
```

```bash
quarto render letter.qmd --to letter-pdf
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | array | required | The recipient's address, one line per entry. |
| `subject` | string | | The subject line. |
| `subject-title` | string | `Subject` | The label before the subject. |
| `subject-suffix` | string | `:` | What follows that label. |
| `opening` | string | | The opening salutation. |
| `closing` | string | | The closing salutation. |
| `cc` | array | | Carbon copy recipients. |
| `encl` | array | | Enclosures. |
| `ps` | string | | A postscript, after the closing. |
| `header-image` | path | | A letterhead, placed above the opening. |
| `header-image-width` | string | `\textwidth` | Its width, as a LaTeX dimension. |
| `signature-image` | path | | A signature, between the closing and the printed name. |
| `signature-image-width` | string | `4cm` | Its width, as a LaTeX dimension. |

: Options under `letter-pdf`. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[24,10,16,50]"}

::: {.callout-note}
Widths are passed to `\includegraphics`, so any LaTeX dimension works: `4cm`, `120pt`, `0.5\textwidth`.

In a double-quoted YAML string the backslash has to be doubled, as `"0.5\\textwidth"`, or the literal is lost.
:::

## Diagnostics

| Condition | Reported as |
| --- | --- |
| `address` missing or empty | An error. |
| `subject-title` set with no `subject` | A warning. |
| `subject` or `subject-title` containing raw HTML such as `<x>` | A warning, since Pandoc strips it from LaTeX output. |

: What the format reports while rendering. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[46,54]"}

## Snippets

The extension ships editor snippets for the front matter: `meta` for an English letter, `meta-fr` for a French one, and `meta-sig` for one with a signature image.
They work in any editor with Quarto's IDE integration.

## Limitations

- PDF only, through LaTeX. HTML waits on Paged.js support in Quarto.
- Image widths are LaTeX dimensions, so they are not portable to a future HTML output as written.
